transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

What finally got me to come in is I can’t seem to keep my focus at work. I’ll be trying to finish one estimate or fill out a code form, and then a tool noise, or a text, or even some idea I get about setting up the workshop pulls me away. Then I come back and I’ve mixed things up between jobs. It’s been getting hard to manage.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have a hard time staying seated when you need to?

Yeah, pretty often. I don’t like just sitting around—it feels like I’m wasting time. I’ll go from job sites to looking at bids, then back home messing with test panels in the workshop. And I keep starting new home-automation projects before I’ve finished the last one. It’s like I need to keep moving or doing something.
Have you had trouble with focus or restlessness for as long as you can remember, or did it start more recently?

It’s more recent. I mean, I’ve always been active, but this trouble focusing and feeling like I can’t settle has really been building over the last seven months or so—since we took on the mortgage for the workshop and equipment.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, like feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?
I don’t know, not really. I wouldn’t say I’ve been hopeless or anything. I get frustrated when I can’t keep things straight, but I haven’t really thought of it as feeling down or losing interest.
